rec.name: PDP Anchor-Link Navigation for Product Details (Expanded Content, Scroll-to-Section)
rec.status: Reference only — spec from a single ticket line with a live example URL; build status unknown

what.text: A navigation on the product page that links to anchor points for the product detail sections (e.g. description, features, materials, size guide). Nothing is collapsed into an accordion or tab. All content stays fully visible on the page, and clicking a nav item scrolls the page down to the matching section. The ticket gives a live example on the dopesnow.com product page for the Blizzard Full-Zip Snowboard Jacket (men's, black).

why.text: Content that is already open removes the click-and-reveal effort that accordions add, so shoppers see the product information (specs, benefits, sizing) without having to hunt for it. The anchor nav gives a quick overview of what is on the page and lets shoppers jump straight to what matters to them, such as fit or material. This reduces friction and uncertainty on long PDPs, and fully visible text also helps content discoverability and SEO. This reasoning is my inference; the ticket does not state it.

how.text: Add a nav row (links or tabs) near the product info or the start of the details area. Each link points to an element id on a content section (href='#section-id'). All detail sections are rendered open, with no accordion or tab collapse. Use smooth scrolling (CSS scroll-behavior: smooth or a small JS handler) and a scroll-margin-top or offset so the target is not hidden under a sticky header. Optionally make the nav sticky and highlight the active section while scrolling. The ticket only states the behavior (no collapsing, scroll to anchor); the implementation details are inferred.

items: Nav items: label and target section (description, details/features, materials, size guide, reviews, etc.)
Scroll offset to account for the sticky header
Show on mobile: horizontal scrollable chip row vs. hidden

dependencies.text: No specific apps or metafields are named in the ticket. Assumes a PDP template with distinct content sections or blocks that can carry unique ids. If the section content is product-specific, it likely comes from the product description or metafields (unconfirmed). The sticky header height must be known for the scroll offset.

items: Click rate on anchor nav items
Size-guide opens or clicks (if a size anchor is included)
